body_long:
Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group has appointed Jonathan Payne as General Manager of Mandarin Oriental, Canouan, its resort in St Vincent and the Grenadines. Hospitality Net published the appointment on 9 November 2026, and the group's own release followed on eHotelier on 11 November. No start date has been given.

## The resort

Mandarin Oriental, Canouan is an all-suite, all-villa resort on Godahl Beach, at Carenage Bay on Canouan Island. Its accommodation ranges from ocean-view suites in a colonial style to Italian-designed Patio Villas, penthouses and signature villas. Guests reach the island on short connecting flights from Barbados, Saint Vincent, St Lucia or Grenada. The resort lists a Michelin Key, a Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star rating and a World Spa Awards title for the Caribbean's best wellness retreat.

## Who is Jonathan Payne

Payne joins from Sugar Beach, A Viceroy Resort, in St Lucia, where he was Resort Manager for nearly four years. During that time the resort collected World Travel Awards, a place in Travel + Leisure's World's Best Awards and a Michelin Key. Before St Lucia, he was Resident Manager at Sandy Lane in Barbados, a Forbes Five-Star and AAA Five Diamond property.

His wider career covers senior roles at luxury hotels and resorts in Bali, Thailand, Mozambique, the Maldives and the United Kingdom, and more than 25 years across the Caribbean, Europe, Africa and Southeast Asia. He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Hotel and Business Management from the University of Gloucestershire.

## The brief

According to the group, Payne will oversee the resort's operations, raise service delivery, develop strategic partnerships and strengthen the resort's position in the market. The release does not include a quote from him or from a group executive.

## The group

Mandarin Oriental operates or is developing 44 hotels, with close to 11,000 rooms in 25 countries, according to the figure carried with the announcement. Canouan is one of its few resorts in the Caribbean, and one of its most remote.

## The signal

In the Caribbean, the leading resorts recruit from a small circuit of islands. Barbados, St Lucia and the Grenadines share the same winter guests, the same staff pool and the same travel advisers. A general manager who knows Sandy Lane and Sugar Beach brings that network with him. For Mandarin Oriental, the choice favours local knowledge over a transfer from inside the group.
